rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose noun for biological life, existence, lifespan in general, or a loved one described as someone’s life.

example.english: This discovery made me appreciate the value of life again.
example.traditional: 呢個發現令我重新感受到生命嘅可貴。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 faat3 jin6 ling6 ngo5 cung4 san1 gam2 sau6 dou3 saang1 ming6 ge3 ho2 gwai3

rows.note: Use this for someone’s everyday life or way of living, including work, family, and other areas of life, and also when “life” means a livelihood.

example.english: After moving to the countryside, my life became much more relaxed.
example.traditional: 搬咗去郊區之後，我嘅生活輕鬆咗好多。
example.jyutping: bun1 zo2 heoi3 gaau1 keoi1 zi1 hau6 ngo5 ge3 saang1 wut6 hing1 sung1 zo2 hou2 do1

rows.note: Use this when counting, losing, or saving individual human or animal lives.

example.english: When fighting the fire, the priority is to save human life.
example.traditional: 救火嗰陣，最緊要係保住人命。
example.jyutping: gau3 fo2 go2 zan6 zeoi3 gan2 jiu3 hai6 bou2 zyu6 jan4 meng6

rows.note: Use this specifically for the length of time a person, organism, or operating object is expected to last.

example.english: The battery's life is longer than I expected.
example.traditional: 部電池嘅壽命比我想像中長。
example.jyutping: bou6 din6 ci4 ge3 sau6 ming6 bei2 ngo5 soeng2 zoeng6 zung1 coeng4
